item.text:
The weights encode **nonmonotonic age and laboratory effects**, not a conventional mortality score. Units 1, 2 and 6 strongly associate severe WFNS grade with higher risk and treatment with lower risk. Unit 3 creates a sharp age-related increase of up to **2.428 log-odds**, superimposed on a frequently decreasing younger-age trend. Units 5 and 8 introduce opposing age–laboratory relationships. Even some CT effects reverse direction.

The surrogate below is an **unvalidated, weight-derived approximation**, targeting roughly ages 20–90, laboratory values 0–10 and broadly balanced binary profiles. Its permitted additive splines and product terms cannot reproduce every moving threshold. Rankings are approximate without a patient distribution; “no clear effect” includes sign-changing effects, not just negligible ones.

Treatment during admission is not genuinely an admission-time predictor; its association is neither causal evidence nor protection against temporal leakage. The weights suggest structured training but cannot establish registry provenance.
